Tired of paying recurring vector database fees and watching your AI coding agent forget everything the moment a context window resets? 🤖💸

Meet OKF Agent Memory: a lightning-fast, zero-dependency Go library that gives your AI coding assistants Git-native persistent memory using local BM25 search. 

By storing everything as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter directly inside your repository, it combines human-readable simplicity with powerful structured retrieval. No black-box infrastructure. No expensive API calls. Just your project context, living right where your code lives. 🚀

⚡ WHY YOU NEED IT:
• Sub-millisecond speed: Concept searches in under 300 microseconds and full corpus graph validation in about 4ms, with an RSS memory footprint under 15MB.
• 100% Git-native: Track architectural decisions, coding standards, and memory states using standard git diff and git log.
• Progressive disclosure: Hierarchical index files and link graphs ensure agents only load the exact concepts they need, completely eliminating token bloat and context rot.
• MCP ready: Native Model Context Protocol server support over stdio out of the box for seamless integration with Claude Code, Cursor, and other modern AI platforms.

Whether you are building autonomous coding workflows or trying to stop your AI assistant from hallucinating outdated patterns across sessions, OKF Agent Memory delivers reliable, low-latency, and cost-effective context management right on your local machine. 🛠️

Check out the repository and drop it into your project today:
https://github.com/okf-memory/okf-agent-memory

Tired of vendor lock-in and black-box limitations with your AI coding assistants? 

Take full control of your AI-assisted development workflows with OpenCode, a high-velocity open-source coding agent designed as a powerful alternative to proprietary tools. 🚀

OpenCode solves the problem of rigid workflows and lack of customization by giving developers a fully open-source, extensible coding agent that operates directly within your terminal and desktop environments to plan, build, and navigate complex codebases.

🔥 Notable Features:
• Dual-Mode Agent System: Seamlessly switch between a full-access build agent and a read-only plan agent for safe code exploration.
• Built-In Subagent Architecture: Handle complex multi-step tasks and deep codebase searches via intuitive commands like @general.
• Cross-Platform & Flexible: Install easily via Homebrew, npm, scoop, choco, or custom directories on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
• Robust Desktop App & TUI: Enjoy a comprehensive desktop application alongside a powerful terminal user interface.

Whether you are safely analyzing legacy architecture without risking accidental file modifications or accelerating multi-file refactoring right from your CLI, OpenCode integrates smoothly into your existing workflow without relying on closed-source platforms. 💻✨

👉 Check it out on GitHub: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode

Stuck on an RTX 30 or RTX 20 series card and missing out on modern DLSS Frame Generation? The hardware capability restriction is finally broken. 🚀

Check out sdli1995/dlssg_for_sm86, a powerful repository that brings advanced frame-generation capabilities to legacy RTX 30 (SM86) and RTX 20 (SM75) series GPUs by natively hosting and routing custom PTX and Cubin inference graphs.

🔥 The Problem It Solves:
Older NVIDIA architectures lack native support for modern DLSS Frame Generation pipelines. This project solves that roadblock by packaging a custom C++ wrapper, model inference graphs, and architecture-specific PTX/Cubin routing directly into a drop-in DLL proxy. It bypasses the need for an installed CUDA Toolkit and eliminates the need to unpack or map original vendor binaries.

⚡ Notable Features:
• Native DLL proxy wrapping model inference graphs and architecture-specific kernels without modifying original vendor files.
• Multi-architecture routing supporting SM86 and SM75 with precise and approximate bilinear sampling configurations.
• Comprehensive frame-generation pipeline management supporting 2X, 3X, and 4X multiplication modes with explicit VRAM budgeting and resource reclamation fixes.
• Robust debugging and diagnostic hooks, including configurable logging levels, digital signing for integrity verification, and alternative DLL entrypoints to bypass loader restrictions.

🛠️ Developer & Engineer Value:
Graphics engineers and developers can study this codebase to master low-level D3D12 proxy layers, API interception, and custom CUDA PTX/Cubin inference execution outside standard vendor frameworks. It is a brilliant reference for writing zero-overhead C++ wrappers, managing manual GPU memory budgets, and routing hardware execution paths across different GPU generations without heavy external runtimes.

Get the code and inspect the architecture here:
https://github.com/sdli1995/dlssg_for_sm86

Stop settling for single-shot AI image and code generation that misses the mark every single time. 

Transform text prompts into production-grade 3D scenes and graphics demos using a closed-loop multi-agent system that critiques and iterates on its own visual output. 

Building interactive 3D web graphics, browser games, or complex Blender assets usually means dealing with brittle zero-shot pipelines that require endless manual tweaks. Dream-loop solves this by establishing a closed-loop multi-agent feedback pipeline. An image generator dreams up a target screenshot, a builder agent implements the code or 3D assets in environments like Three.js or Blender, and a separate critic agent evaluates the live output against the target to drive continuous programmatic iteration until visual quality thresholds are met.

Here is what you get out of the box:
• Closed-loop visual iteration where a critic subagent compares live application or scene screenshots against a target reference image to provide actionable feedback.
• Target evolution loop allowing the system to recursively generate progressively better visual targets based on the current state of the application.
• Deep integration with 3D and graphics pipelines, supporting Blender MCP or scripting interfaces alongside web-based technologies like Three.js.
• Autonomous execution designed for advanced AI agents with vision input, image generation capabilities, and subagent orchestration.

Whether you are an AI engineer, creative technologist, frontend developer, or 3D graphics programmer, this project lets you implement self-correcting agent architectures that autonomously debug visual rendering, fix graphical artifacts, and hit strict performance metrics.

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/achimala/dream-loop

Tired of paying for expensive SaaS tools like OpusClip? This open-source AI pipeline turns long YouTube videos into viral vertical shorts locally for free. 🚀

If you are tired of monthly subscriptions eating into your margins, Colafornia/short-video-generator-AI is the local automation tool you need. It handles the end-to-end pipeline of converting long-form YouTube videos or local files into viral vertical shorts without relying on expensive cloud subscriptions.

Here is what it does under the hood:
- Smart Highlight Selection: Uses LLMs like OpenAI, Gemini, or MuAPI to analyze transcripts through a virality framework, scoring emotional peaks, hooks, and conflict to pick the top moments.
- Local Transcription: Leverages faster-whisper locally with flexible device acceleration (CPU or CUDA) for fast, cost-effective timestamped transcripts.
- Flexible Interfaces: Provides both a powerful CLI for automation scripts and a local web interface for visual queueing and rendering management.
- API Support: Allows developers to natively embed the generator into their own internal pipelines and custom applications.

Why AI engineers and developers love it:
You can bypass restrictive SaaS subscriptions and API paywalls by running a completely self-hosted, modular video content engine. The clean separation between the LLM provider, transcription engine, and rendering logic makes it easy to fork, customize the highlight scoring prompt, or hook the core script into automated cron jobs for hands-off social media syndication. 

Whether you are building an automated YouTube-to-TikTok content repurposing pipeline that runs daily on your homelab or integrating the generator API into a custom dashboard for a content agency, this modular engine gives you full control.

Check out the repository and drop a star to support open-source AI:
